result.title: AnachroBench: Evaluating Historical Consistency in Large Vision-Language Models
result.summary: Existing Large Vision-Language Model benchmarks primarily evaluate visual understanding in general everyday scenarios, leaving historical consistency with a specified era and country largely underexplored. To address this gap, we propose AnachroBench, a controlled discriminative benchmark for evaluating historical consistency in visual scenes. It contains 1,600 image pairs from eight countries spanning the late 19th to the early 20th century, each pairing an original historical image with an anachronistic version containing a seamlessly inserted modern object. AnachroBench evaluates three aspects: Inserted Object Perception, which tests whether models detect the inserted modern object; Era-Country Consistency, which assesses whether the scene is consistent with the specified era and country; and Conditional Era-Country Consistency, which measures consistency judgments only when the inserted object is correctly perceived. A false consistency judgment occurs when a model perceives the modern object but still judges the scene as historically consistent. Overall, AnachroBench reveals a gap between inserted object perception and era-country consistency judgments, providing a targeted evaluation of this behavior.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 AnachroBench，一个受控判别式基准：用 8 国 19 世纪末至 20 世纪初的 1600 对历史图像（原图与无缝插入现代物体的版本）评估 VLM 的插入物体感知、时代—国家一致性及条件一致性判断。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「感知到现代物体却仍判场景历史一致」的发现直接对应 VLM 是否真正使用视觉证据、是否存在视觉旁路，可供核查 LVR 中的证据筛选与答案贡献分配；但未涉及 latent 状态，关联偏诊断层面。
